prompt:
Use case: scientific-educational. Paint ONE definitive full-body human anatomical teaching model as a harmonious naturalistic 1800s medical atlas plate, isolated on fully transparent background. Tall portrait composition, complete crown to toes with comfortable margins. This is one real anatomically continuous adult body, never a collage of organ pictures. Reference1 establishes thoracic anatomy and engraved watercolor style; reference2 establishes the built arm bones, shoulder girdle and biceps/triceps; reference3 establishes one continuous brain, spinal cord and vertebral column; reference4 establishes the connected digestive tract; reference5 establishes paired kidneys, ureters and bladder. Repaint these anatomical relationships into ONE organism at adult scale; do not paste or shrink reference rectangles.
Adult standing natural anatomical pose, front view with head turned slightly toward viewer's right so a supported cranial/ear cutaway can be seen. Correct classical human proportions about7.5heads tall, shoulders about2.5head widths, realistic broad pelvis and continuous waist, hands reaching mid-thigh, elbows near waist, normal long forearms and complete hands/feet. Arms relaxed slightly away from sides, palms mostly forward, knees relaxed but legs straight. Quiet neutral face, dignified medical model, no theatrical gesture. Keep anatomical left/right convention: liver at viewer-left, stomach viewer-right, heart apex viewer-right. Smooth modest clinical groin without emphasized genitals.
Retain natural pale skin on most head/limbs, with one BROAD CONTINUOUS anatomically edged opening from upper chest to pelvis revealing existing chest and abdominal anatomy. Side rib arcs and intercostal walls sit INSIDE the body silhouette. Preserve the upper manubrium and continuous clavicles reaching its sternoclavicular joints; remove lower central anterior ribs/sternum to open the thorax. The clavicles and scapular supports genuinely attach both arms. Paired lungs flank a fist-size oblique heart, pulmonary vessels enter both lung hila alongside bronchi, normal heart cutaway, diaphragm shallow domes beneath lungs/heart. BELOW diaphragm the liver and stomach contact its underside, gut fills the abdominal cavity naturally, colon frames small-intestinal loops. The thorax tapers continuously into abdomen and broad pelvis; no ledge, hanging rib-panel edge, pinched waist or disconnected organ pouch. Two kidneys lie posterior-lateral in upper abdomen, partially visible beside the digestive organs, two ureters descend to a small bladder low in pelvis. Urinary and digestive outlets stay distinct. The esophagus remains continuously routed from throat behind airway/heart through diaphragm into stomach, visible only where its depth permits; no floating duplicate tube.
Expose one cranial side in a supported skull cutaway: brain inside skull, one natural-size eye seated in orbit, optic nerve into brain; one continuous ear preparation with outer ear/canal/ossicles/cochlea and balance apparatus embedded in temporal bone, no detached magnification. ONE spinal column and spinal cord descend posterior to organs, predominantly occluded at normal depth; fine pale peripheral nerves exit between vertebrae and continue toward limbs. No second spine drawn down front of body. A natural arm window on viewer's LEFT exposes humerus, biceps in front and triceps behind, elbow joint, forearm bones and normal tendons, with supplied supporting muscle. Their shoulder origins and collarbone meet the chest continuously. Other arm remains anatomically ordinary. Fine lymphatic channels remain embedded in lateral tissue planes, with a subtle thoracic duct and its real left jugular-subclavian venous junction; no hanging lymph-tree overlay, detached vein stump or branching yellow ornament across lungs.
On the skin of viewer's LEFT forearm below the muscle window, show one modest short healed pale-pink linear scar, flush with continuous normal skin. It is a skin surface, not a square pasted histology block. Cutaway borders follow natural tissue contours, no chopped rectangular windows. Fine sepia copperplate hatching, restrained rose muscle/viscera, ivory bone, muted madder arteries, slate-blue veins, pale gold nerves, very restrained straw lymph. Sophisticated legible physician-office anatomical poster. No text, labels, numbers, arrows, captions, inset organs, detached pieces, multiple views, paper rectangle, border, shadow or stand.
